title: Trump: Roy Cohn introduces Roger Stone to Donald Trump (and Fred Trump)
description_short: Trump: Roy Cohn introduces Roger Stone to Donald Trump (and Fred Trump)
description_medium: The Trump File timeline says Roy Cohn arranged Roger Stone’s first meeting with Donald Trump sometime in 1979. Stone was then running Ronald Reagan’s campaign organization across New York, New Jersey and Connecticut and was looking for office space. Trump discussed Reagan’s path to 270 electoral votes, then sent Stone to his father, Fred Trump.
description_long: According to the Trump File timeline quoting Roger Stone, Roy Cohn arranged Stone’s first meeting with Donald Trump sometime in 1979. Stone was then running Ronald Reagan’s campaign organization in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut and looking for office space. Cohn told him to make a pitch to Trump. Stone recalled Trump asking how Reagan could reach 270 electoral votes before agreeing to help and directing Stone to his father, Fred. Stone said he visited Fred Trump at the family’s Avenue Z office in Coney Island. He recalled receiving $200,000 in $1,000 checks made payable to Reagan for President, which he described as legal bundling, a way to collect many individual contributions. The episode, as Stone later recounted it, connects his early political work to the Trump family and shows how Cohn helped open that relationship. The page’s timeline heading assigns the event to July 1, but its narrative gives only the year. It also speculates that Trump met Paul Manafort soon afterward because Stone and Manafort became business partners in 1980; that inference does not establish when Trump and Manafort first met.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Roy Cohn introduces Roger Stone to Donald Trump (and Fred Trump)
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Roy Cohn introduces Roger Stone to Donald Trump (and Fred Trump)

notes: The linked timeline’s heading assigns July 1, 1979, while its narrative dates the meeting only to sometime in 1979. The account attributes the sequence and fundraising details to Stone; it speculates, rather than documents, when Trump first met Paul Manafort. The descriptions use the year and omit that inference.
proposed_correction: Roy Cohn Arranged a 1979 Meeting Between Roger Stone and Donald Trump

title: Trump: Robert Maxwell tells Israel about nuclear weapons whistleblower
description_short: Trump: Robert Maxwell tells Israel about nuclear weapons whistleblower
description_medium: In September 1986, Mordechai Vanunu brought photographs of an Israeli nuclear facility to British newspapers, including Robert Maxwell’s Sunday Mirror, according to the linked timeline. A separate New York Times headline later reported Israel had confirmed it was holding Vanunu. The timeline alleges Maxwell passed information to Israel, but the available material does not document that contact.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Robert Maxwell tells Israel about nuclear weapons whistleblower
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Robert Maxwell tells Israel about nuclear weapons whistleblower

notes: Reason: The Trump File timeline alleges that Maxwell informed Israel about Vanunu, but the Times link returned 403 and its headline does not establish Maxwell’s contact. Proposed correction: provide a source documenting the alleged communication or retitle the entry around Vanunu’s disclosure and Israel’s confirmation that it held him.
proposed_correction: Robert Maxwell Accused of Alerting Israel to Nuclear Whistleblower Mordechai Vanunu

description_medium: Project 2025’s education agenda included proposals concerning the Department of Education, civil-rights enforcement, curriculum and school funding. The sources do not document a requirement for teachers or principals to sign loyalty oaths, or an educator-specific Schedule F policy.

title: Violence Against Women Act Defunding - Domestic Violence Support Elimination

title: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
description_short: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
description_medium: Russia seized Crimea in 2014 and held a referendum under its control during the wider Ukraine crisis. The linked Trump File timeline asserts that Paul Manafort helped Russia take the territory, but does not describe his actions or offer evidence for the claim. The cited Vox explainer covers the crisis and referendum without establishing Manafort’s role.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine

notes: Reason: The linked Trump File page asserts that Manafort helped Russia control Crimea but gives no details; the cited Vox explainer covers the Ukraine crisis and referendum without documenting his role. Proposed correction: supply a source naming Manafort’s specific actions and how they aided the takeover, or remove the unsupported attribution and Trump connection.
proposed_correction: Russia Seizes Crimea in 2014; Manafort’s Role in the Event Is Unclear

title: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda
description_short: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda
description_medium: An expert on the Internet Research Agency told a reporter that some social-media accounts which had promoted Russian forces in Ukraine appeared to shift toward pro-Trump messages in December 2015. The linked timeline attributed the observation to those account patterns and said they appeared connected to Russian operators. It names no accounts and does not verify who controlled them.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda

notes: Reason: The linked timeline attributes the alleged shift to an unnamed journalist and says the accounts only appeared tied to Russian operators; it provides no handles, platform evidence, or operator verification. Proposed correction: identify the accounts and the evidence for their control, or keep the claim explicitly attributed and provisional.
proposed_correction: Report Says Some Accounts Promoting Russian Actions in Ukraine Shifted to Pro-Trump Messaging

title: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
description_short: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
description_medium: By May 22, 2026, Trump was considering possible additional strikes on Iran. A New York Times report listed energy facilities, the underground nuclear site at Isfahan, and missile sites as potential targets. Reuters had earlier reported that Trump said the United States might need to strike again. Both reports describe options under discussion, not a new strike order.
subcategory: Reported consideration of possible further strikes on Iran

preserved_fields.title: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
preserved_fields.description_medium: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran. There is no shortage of targets if he decides to strike: Energy facilities left untouched, the deep underground nuclear storage site at Isfahan and missile sites that appear to have been dug out. This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.

notes: Reason: The Times and Reuters pages returned HTTP 403 and 401 during focused retrieval. Their supplied headlines identify possible targets and consideration of another strike, but no decision, timeline or outcome. Proposed correction: keep the entry framed as options under consideration unless a source documents a strike order or action.
proposed_correction: Trump Weighs Possible Further Strikes on Iran; Source Text Needed
